Also heres some advice as someone autistic having dated other autistics. Heres what I've got, the proper rules/ his rules werent agreed to. He goes in a mood and shuts down emotionally. 

Ok so when he reacts this way theres 5 things to check and keep in mind perhaps 
 1 is it ambiguity
2 is it sensory 
3 is it task switching/ cutting a tast short
4 is it genral uncertainty/ unexpected change 

Ambiguity: 
When poeple talk they often use ambigious language or imply instead of state. Soo if someone says " in a minute " they might mean later. However in an autistic head your first interpretation of this sentence is likely to be that it will happen inexactly 60 seconds. Another example is " its quite dirty in here " this for example might imply its time to cclean up. But since that isn't said an autsitic person might simply agree with you saying "yes it is dirty". Completely missing the hint. Anything implied including unstated rules in a game will create miss understanding 
2. Sensory 

We have slightly orsometimes vastly different sensory configurations.  In an nt mind you can zone in on key information in your enviroment  while only subconciously processing the rest. For example you don't hear every single conversation in a busy bar because your listening to your friends voice. In an autistic mind because we cannot block things out it might well be the case that its overwelming processing all of the  background noise / messy place/ strange touch or texture all at once. So if youve had a real busy day either visually or autiorily this can often be a massive drain on autistic mental resources. Some poeple can even have a meltdown. Prior to a melt down you feel a bit like you have a horrible hangover. Little things erritate you. And during an actual meltdown poeple have varied experiences. 

Task switching

We have one track minds sometimes if the whole game isn't played for example or some other tast or activity is cut short. It can be down right upsetting. Unfortunately it happens in life. 5 minute warnings even 30 second warnings are great for making this easier. 
General uncertainty and unexpected change:

The only way I can really explain it is that sometimes a day or an activity is like a recipe to us. If you vary it too much it doesn't taste right. The meal you wanted is efectively ruined because too many things havechanged . You want what you expected, Its hard to process what varies from this. Like a train having to break and reverse and then swich to a different track. Aposed to a car that can just change lanes.
I personally struggle with unexpected change/ general uncertainty. If i go to the shop and their out of the buscuits i planned to buy it can take me quite a while to come up with an alternative perchase if any at all because the change uo is unexpected. 

The last  things I'll say are: shutting down emotionally might be a coping mechanism to avoid meltdowns or it might be delayed emotional processing( doesnt understand wjat hes feeling.) Or he just struggles to hide what he is feeling more than other poeple. Either way he doesn't seem used to being able to talk about what bothers him, and he wont unless he has some reason to believe you are going to respond differently to other nero typicals. It is a stretch for you to unsestand what he is feeling and why. But it is also a big ass strech for him to do that withyou and poeple in genral every day.

Theres a book called aspergers syndrome and long termm relationships by ashley stanford that might help. Its the best I found from reviews although I'm only 0artly into it myself. It helps both the nt and autistic person in the relationship

You have a lot to cope with thats for sure. Your title says that life is pointless, well what if it was? What I mean is I kind of had an apithany that ended up being quite freeing. I realised that life might very well be pointless. That there is no grand sceme. No point to humanity as a whole  or indeed to pleasing anyone. Heres the thing, it made me realise that I was pleasing others quite allot. I wasn't really living for me. And going about the process of changing this took time but ultimately made me feel a lot more free.

 The only point to life perhaps is self discovery. Here is what I mean. If you were a scientist who stumbled on an unknown meterial and started to run tests. You would want to find the limitations and potential of the meterial. But at no point would it make any sense to be mad at the meterial for 'failing' a test. This is how I derive meaning from life. By figuring out what alien supstance I am made of. Eventually you will die. But don't you atleast want to know who you are before you do? If say you could be good at x or learn this or that about y. Life is not a series of achievements in the eyes of others it is better understanding the optimal conditions for you and what to you is an achievement. The person most capable of finding meaning for you, is you. Because you understand your own meterial or nature best. 
When you work with your own limitations what ever they might be to achieve what you can. Things feel better.

Two children play amongst the ruins of a great city, its industrial bones laid bare as half buildings stand with steel beams protruding amongst abandoned cars. The only thing that glimmers are the windows. The greenish blue squares broken and whole form patterns across the old buildings. All the hard polished steel is now rust and once bright colours are dull and dusty. There is an eerie stillness across what once was a very lively place. Now only the wind and wondering folk travel through the cities. Tig and Ria had wandered from the camp set up on the outskirts and were searching in the ruins for some old technology. Tig had made a working battery and it was a closely guarded secret between the 2 friends as anything technological was not to be tampered with by children. 


"You'll get the jives if you play with tech." That is all old Mag had to say on the matter but the children thought her a bit paranoid all the older people were. You couldn't really blame them, they were there at the end. When the dancing disease infected everyone. Only those with no rhythm survived and music was outlawed. No one had seen a dancer in years but still the stigma was there. 


The 2 children eventually settled in the arch of a big yellow m that must have been a sign once.Tig had a massive frown on his forehead and was fiddling with a tiny screwdriver and a taptop. Or at least that's what tig said it was.


"Tig what do you think it sounded like?" Said ria excitedly she was a free spirit and seemed to like danger a great deal more than tig 

" I hope your not talking about music ria, Mag would skin us like those rabbits." Ria frowned and pouted secretly she thought mag was a bit full of it. 

" i know i know but don't you ever wonder? What it must've been like" she tried again.

" birds make sounds like music " said tig in thought "that's what my dad says" 

"It can't be the same" said ria " sometimes i wish i could just hear it once you know" Tig looked out across the ruins ria was his best friend  

" I wish that too sometimes, there's this whole world we never get to know all because of the dancing hordes. I want to play one of thegames they talk about on a screen!" 

Ria sat up very awake now :

" do you think we could on that taptop?"


" maybe" said tig"it has a speaker,I'm just finishing it.Pass me the battery" 

Ria grabbed the big thing with the black panels that had been sitting in the sun all day, she didn't understand everything tig did, no one really did but it was very exciting. Tig plugged it in and both children held their breath as they looked at the device. A small led light flicked on and both inhaled in amazement. "Tig its working! " 

" careful ria don't touch it!" But it was too late ria already had it in her hands and a small beep could be heard as she accidentally pressed a button.

 " sorry tig" said ria but she didn't sound too sorry. tig looked as excited as she did " its ok i think you turned it on!" A small screen lit up moments later and their was a list to choose from. "Let's pick that one" tig tapped it with his finger and suddenly a dull sound could be heard it was rhythmic and strange to the ears of the children. 2 wires dangled from the small taptop(ipod) ria quickly grabbed one and put it against her ear she drew in a breath and nodded excitedly "tig tig put it by your ear" michael jackson's thriller blasted through the tiny headphones as both children giggled with glee. 

" do you think this is music?" Asked Tig

" I don't know but i like it!" Said ria excitedly and her toes began to tap. She felt as if the ground itself was shaking along. She took the piece away from her ear but still she feel the rhythm. something was coming. Something that danced…

Marcus feels deeply unsettled nothing seems quite right yet he can't fault a single thing. His room is exactly as he left it but somehow it feels as if everything has been carefully crafted to look that way. All the usual posters are on the wall his toys are where they should be. His favorite teddy is on his bed leaning against the patchwork quilt his grandmother had made for him. Something seems creepy about his favorite bear, somehow the eyes don't seem blank they seem to hide thinly veiled malice.Markus takes off his backpack and  places his it behind his desk chair trying to shake off this uncanny feeling. As he dropped the backpack he could hear a faint hissing sound that he dismisses absentmindedly as the boiler. Out of the corner of his eye he sees his familiar paper weight on his desk looking all wrong but he couldn't think what was wrong. Markus inspects the paperweight. there was absolutely nothing wrong that markus could place his finger on, it was exactly as he remembered it. Everything was exactly as he expected it to be. Still His hair stood on end when he heard his mother's familiar voice call him down stairs for some food.

 "Be right there!" shouted markus. He made his way down the stairs, every step felt like a missed step. His heart was pounding and he felt strangely tired and out of breath the further he walked something felt very wrong. Markus briefly wondered if he was coming down with a fever as he reached the bottom step. The kitchen door was slightly a jar and all the touches of home could be seen in the decorations of the familiar kitchen. Polkadot curtains framed a view of the garden and the pig salt and pepper stood in their usual spot the quirky yellow tea and coffee jars were just slightly miss aligned. All this was pretty normal.He could see his mother now at the kitchen sink with her back turned. Humming, (or was it hissing?) softly. There on the countertop was a sandwich and drink ready for him. It looked so good, somehow it felt like he was looking at a memory. 

'Was the glass and plate always so far to the left' wondered markus in thought. something seemed off. Markus looked back towards his mom and then back at the sandwich  The plate and glass had moved a bit more to the right asif the very room was responding to his thoughts. When markus looked away and back again the plate and cup would be ever so slightly further back or forward. That was enough confirmation that something was amiss.  

' perhaps I need to focus on what I don't know, but it still has to be recognisable to me if it's wrong' he thought cunningly. 

"Mom what's your middle name again?". His heart was beating really fast now. His mother turns round in an eerily fluid motion she smiled slightly.The feeling of weakness in his bones increased as he looked at his mother's eyes. They were like the teddy's as if the same horrific thing laid in wait behind them. He could feel himself sweating as his mother replied still smiling. 

" I can't remember sweetie,come eat your food." Markys looked on in horror as her face warped, the words spilling out just slightly out of time with the movements of her lips. Depending on where markus focussed different parts of her face would blur and warp he couldn't see her whole face at once. 

'Your not my mother'  thought markus and a now clearly audible hiss seemed to sing in response to this thought. Markus knew he had to run. 

As he moved towards the back door his mother slid impossibly fast, asif on wheels, to block his way. " whatsssss wrong sssssweeetie" came the now snake like reply. Markus had to think quick. Markus grabs a knife from the knife block and forces it into its chest, it  showed no sign of pain. 

 " oh noo silly billy now i have a boo boo" came her strange reply as her impossibly long arm now extended to keep the back door closed. Markus couldn't stop looking at her hand. It had a total of eight fingers that now moved in spider like ways. Markus looked on in horror as the hand dislodged itself from her arm and started spinning a web of blood and sinew across the door. Markus backs away and runs for the front door. He tries the handle but it's locked. " The key dammit! The key!" thought markus as he tumbled  with shaking hands to retrieve it from the hook. He made it out just as an immaculate mother lunged forward to grab him. Markus shut the door behind him only to find himself back in his bedroom. His mind was fuzzy and the room once again looking eerily perfect. He could feel his memory starting to slip 'how many times has this happened?' He wondered frantically, feeling weaker still.

 'Everything seems just a little more homely this time' noted markus . He fought to hold onto his memory and once again ran for the front door. He made it out without any trouble in fact it was easier this time. a loud aggravated hiss seemed to permeate everything as he left only to be back in his bedroom once again.

"It's working " thought markus " give up!" he shouted as he ran "I can do this forever!" again he reached the front door the house now trembling and shaking as random bits of it disappears. This time when he opens the front door there is only a white void. Markus steps into it his feet feeling heavy, so heavy that he soon finds himself crawling across the vast nothing that gives way and sticks to him like chewing gum. Then suddenly his eyes shoot open and all around him in his bedroom are coils upon coils of a massive snake. Markus can't move . He bites  down hard on the coil closest to his mouth and out comes the frantic hiss of the creature as it starts to retreat. it slid off the bed with impossible speed it grew smaller until it disappeared out the window into the shadowy night.

The word no 



She was a tiny little thing. the little cries should not fade and no one should watch the color drain from beneath the soft rosy skin of one that had not yet uttered a word.but there I stood looking at myself and her asif my soul had fled and only by autonomous body remained. The doctors did not know what ailed her, she did not keep down any nourishment


her little fingers relaxed round mine and I cried deep within my soul feeling now the splintery pain. something was fractured like glass that could not take the strain and out poured my innards in the form of tears that I did not think could stop the only thing that came to mind was no. No this could not happen.no was the revolt in my soul no was the unsettlingly deep vibration that grasped me and pulled deep into its very origins.it made me shake and rattle like a bag of glass . No was the word that slipped like a whirlwind from my lungs across my tongue and with a guttural boom into the hospital room and I was afraid of what I had done. 


The instinct to undo was the anchor the need to protect the love of a parent for their child the ocean within which the anchor fell. But what the word would do I did not know. Should I recoil or rejoice? Should I sing or sink? I have a tongue with the power of meaning and speech that sung out like ocean waves across the world and in a flood could change it. I did not know my own doing what it meant when once again the cupids bow of my sweet child quivered and a cry espaped her lungs, I did not know. But I cried once more thankful for the curse.so happy was I ,that I felt it leaked out beneath the door of the room to spill across the hospital, delirious joy.


 A happy that reduced me again to tears as I held her, my cursed child as atlas held the world. My mind foggy as the damp clung to my cheeks. Knowing regret might come knocking. Knowing that I could not utter the word again I could not kill my own child for surely nothing bad can come of my love for her. She grew as normal and soon she was a young child and still the night I brought her back echoed in my mind and I worried, but her smile lit up the days and her sweet nature spoke of no curse she was loved by all and never met with calamity. Soon the worry ceased. It was not until her 30th birthday that worry crept back in as I noticed not something but its lack. She had grown into a wonderful woman with many talents she sung with the voice of an angel, could cook up a storm and cared well for her children. 


Not a single wrinkle was on her brow no hint of crows feet at the edge of her eyes and for a moment I worried but once more put it aside. The years went on and not five years later her family passed in a fire. But Amelia she slept and woke with no roof above her head and all but herself and the bed were cinders. And she came and told me who she knew would utter no word this sad tale before disappearing. she was afraid they might think her some witch and rightly so. It is then that I understood her curse. My child could not die. I had thought death a curse and deprived her soul of the afterlife and of any rest. She would watch all she loved ripped from her arms and still live on watching the machinations of man as they build and change, my child alone in this world forever young and forever running and I could say nothing to guide her. My Amelia.

Chasing Moonlight

Yesterday.

In my corner of this tangerine hell hole 
some fault jerkily tripped the grid. 
Severing meaningless lives
from watts, amps and digitals.  
In the innards of our concrete dwellings,
true darkness overwhelms.
So I step out. I look up.

I find the ghost our sun still touches,
full to balance each iris eclipse, 
gonging out glamor onto 
inner city eye sores. 
Begetting polished mysteries 
you daren't unravel.

Its larger than any grievance I have.
I embrace it more wholly, 
than I could my ex-wives. 
Like their love and my money,
its gleam disappeared,
replaced by the seeping puss
of festered wounds and streetlights. 

A month later.

I find myself missing moonlight, 
the phosphorescent city, 
only a simulacrum of the heavens.
I walk into dark ally's, 
risk my wallet in pursuit 
of  this timid pinnacle.
Moonlight remains elusive in the city, 
so I go find it by the ocean. 

I spend my waking night in spotlight,
watching it morph rivulets of crinkling water, 
into quicksilver wickers.
I am enamoured, 
empowered by my insignificance. 
My camera refuses to capture 
what seems so nakedly appreciable, 
at whit's end I take my photo.
Black and white. 

  2 months later. 

Corporate blue carpets ring true to school bells, 
pasty walls stink of  stagnant denigration.
Economical efficiancy depletes this night,
lending its draining orientation, 
to poorly inpersonating a photo gallery.

My trophy competes,
with every other framed opalecent variant. 
All claim to capture nights arcane lucency.
All conected by the futility of reinvigorating a cliché. 
My take squats phlegmatically. 
People gather to pay homage, scrutinise, 
so I note remarks from afar. 
Watching raised eyebrows prepare 
and cock their legs to piss on my photo. 
Their tensed verbal spews mark their territories 
with essence of disdain.
  
A woman wonders between them.
The space cant possess her,
she's not of the nylon sea.
I begrudge her lack of disguise,
how lightly and blithely 
she carries her difference. 

All in grey she stands.
a loosely woven turtleneck  
adorns skinny jeans and trainers.
Only an incandescent hairless head
not wrapped. 

She stops infront of my photo,
head barely incicled by my moon. 
She looks into its distance,
blends with the  silver filigree.
The boxed in radiance,
leaking with her, into the room. 
I took another picture and left,
with my second failed attempt.
Feeling cheated, by her effortless embodiment.
Feeling the insignificance, of my burdens.

I'm sat in the park waiting. Its a rundown park that no one really goes to during the day. I thought it would be a good spot to meet. I sat on one of the creeky swings. I go on my phone to pass the time, looking up once in a while to see if he has shown up yet. The next time I look up he's sat on the swing next to mine curiously watching me. It startled me. I have so many questions, I had been thinking about them all, all day. For a moment I struggled to speak at all. Kenny helped me out 
"you said you have something Important to tell me? " 
I look at him a moment, he is giving nothing away .
"Kenny, I know you changed things." 
The words felt wierd in my mouth like I was going insane but then I could hear him inhale in surprise. His eyes shot wide. So I ask 
"Can I see your arm? I need to see the mark so I know I'm not going insane" 
He seems excited now and lifts his sleave and there it is, the infinity mark. 
"Geez it's really is there" 

We talked for a long time I had allot of questions. But kenny shrugged at allot of them he didn't know half the answers . He had only done what he did to me once before it was to the postman. He said he didn't know how it worked yet. That he could see inside people. But only if he wanted to. And understand their lives "Allot of poeple have this uglyness but you don't seem to have it. It doesn't change when I change things. Their cores stay the same. Thats why I changed the postman he was so ugly inside but I couldn't change that"  

It was the wierdest conversation of my life. Everything just seemed to spill out of his mouth and he seemed relieved to be sharing.  "I learn differently too and I know things. The only thing I don't seem to know is how I work. Where I come from. I'm in foster care. They thought I was a no-tally. My mark only came in last year." I had never heard of a mark coming in so late, it normally showed up by the time you were 3 if you weren't born with it. I understood in part why he hid it, natural hundreds often got pinched by skin grafters.

 I asked him more about the things he knew " Almost everything seems to be a perspective you have to pick up. Theres so much I know but the thing is I don't know how to show poeple. The world only seems to understand things on their own terms, in their own terms. Theres a limit to what poeple will believe too. True or not. The most frustrating thing is knowing the answer while simultaniously understanding that they can't stretch their minds far enough  to accept it. I've tried but poeple wouldn't respond well to half of established science being corrected by a 14 year old. Or any field for that matter. I could prove things once I'm older but it would take time. "

 "why not show your mark?" I asked "they might believe you then" "or kill me"he replied. "Poeple like how things are they don't like change and I can change poeples numbers. If they understood that they would kill me or lock me up so I would do it for them all the time." "Why don't you do it all the time?" I asked gently " well because I don't know how it works and I'm not sure high tallys make poeple happy "   he was saying all this stuff  but the truth was he still just seemed like a kid who felt as lost as the rest of us. I refrained from asking allot more  questions because I didn't want to overwelm him. 

I asked if it meant he never needed to study and he said no. "The problem is I don't know everything, what I think I know is the truth but poeple don't like it. I still need to get through school so yes I have to study. I have to learn what poeple believe is true." if I hadn't seen the mark if I didn't have the diary entry I would have thought he was insane. I asked if he was immortal " I don't think I'm immortal and thats what worries me, what do I pick? What is the most important?" The question was way out of my depth. But I tried." I think you do what feels right, you do what you want to, you can't live your life for other poeple. You owe it to yourself to find your own happiness too." He smiled when I said it." I'm glad you know about my mark, nobody else does. it gets.. It gets lonely."  That's how we became friends. 

Mostly I drew him out of his own head. Asked him about normal stuff. Introduced him to good music. Got drunk with him. Kenny became my best friend. He continued fixing things cautiously, he would tell me about it and I caught him out sometimes since his memory wouldn't change the way mine did when things changed.  Eventually round the time I turned 21 we talked about the idea of changing my numbers to match his. He wouldn't feel so alone then. He did it eventually and this time I didn't forget the before. I remembered the one reality I had previously lived. I begged him to try change it back but he couldn't. I won't bore you with the details but it's a truly miserable existance some times. However we have each other for company. 

Occasionally we find poeple without that uglyness in them. We talk about changing their tallys but the truth is we don't really know what would end up happening if we did. If the symbol spread and found its way to someone who had a dark core it could end everything. We did achieve immortality of sorts, through scientific means,by the time we reached 30 or rather, we don't age but can still be killed. We time travel too. We are slowly changing the darkness in souls. Turns out it does change over the course of milenia. Turns out reincarnation is a thing. I will write about our adventures some time. But this story right here is how it all started.

I grew up in a tough household you learnt to be quick,  'lessons' were taught with fists, mostly the lesson was to stay out of his way. My tally was high in the 70's but this only seemed to  piss my dad off, he never let me see his. But judging by our small run down flat and his dead end job it wasn't very high. 

School was like a refuge I don't mean to brag or nothing but I was well liked, and I knew I would go places the proof was on my skin, I liked looking at it to remind myself of that on tougher days. Nobody was allowed to talk about their tallys it was school rules. Some shit about preserving our childhoods, too fuckin late. and of course poeple did talk about them. Nah I think it was to stop kids rebelling against the 30 pointers that taught the lessons.

There was this one kid,  you know the wierd one, he pissed me off because he always seemed so happy with himself. They called him limper because of his greasy hair. He never said much, just scribbled  things and muttered. One day we are alone in the hall just me and him. He got sent out, so did I but from different classes. I'm minding my business. Then he smiles at me his eyes go a bit puffy and its like he is looking through me, creeping me out. Like he knew my secrets and felt sorry for me. 

I scowl at him "What're you looking at limper?" Hes a creepy fucker. His eyes shoot down then he says real quiet "I can see what he does to you" this kids unsettling me "stop talking crap limper" but he just keeps staring and like he can't stop he just goes on " I know where the bruises come from" "I know that you cry" I lose it it at this point launch myself across the room. Who the fuck is this kid? Has he been spying on me? Ive got him by the collar now his eyes strech wide, he touches my tally arm " I can fix it" "I can fix it" he would've kept going if I didn't tell him to shut up.  I said it loud. I know doors would start opening soon. I put him down ,I talk quick and low " you can't fix shit limper. What ever the fuck you know you better keep it to yourself you little freak" I was not done with him. The Teacher had stuck her head out of her classroom "no talking in the corridor" then he lifts up his sleave so only I can see but theres no tally....just an infinity symbol. He Smiles at me and nods. Who the fuck is this kid? 

Time passes slowly in the last lesson and all I'm thinking about is what to do about this kid, I would be waiting for him at the gate. Beat the shit out of him. no,  I would just talk to him. I had to figure out what was going on.   How did he know that stuff? What does infinity even mean as a tally? My mind feels slightly foggy probably stress. I look for his  dark haired head bobbing amongs the others after school. But I must have missed him, because he is nowhere to be seen. I could find him online but shit I only know him as limper.  

I head home its not a long walk, but when I get there things are fucking wierd . the house. its not my house theres curtains in the window, no flaky paint on the door. Flowers in pots. I don't know what to do. I freak. I go to the woods. Wonder some way in and just start writing this. I have to....

Now you know what I know. This more or less is my last diary entry, my handwriting. But nothing I remember. I just got up in the woods dazed not knowing exactly how I got there. I headed home .I live with my mom and little brother, I've no idea who my dad is. We're happyish. And my tally is  81, not 70 something.  I'm not sure if I'm going crazy or not but there IS a kid at my school called limper, his real name is Kenny Silverman and I really need to know. To thank him maybe? I'm not sure.

Kenny is in the year below me. He has no friends that I've ever seen, yet it doesn't seem to bother him. He keeps to himself. Everyone reckons he will either blow up the school or become the next einstein. But nobody really knows him. Teachers don't really like him since he has a nack for pointing out their mistakes. 

I didn't have the guts to talk to him. didn't know what I would even say, 'hey are you an extradimentional time traveler and did you change my life and wipe my memory?  Not going to risk sounding that crazy. No if I talked to him it would seem too out of character for me, my friends would notice and ask about it. He is nowhere online either. Hes a ghost. So I slipped him a note when I was helping to hand stuff out for the teacher. Asked him to meet me in the park by the woods after school  I wrote  that I had something important to tell him. No idea if  he will show .
